brief: A desk CO2 monitor with a small screen and a light that goes green to red, powered by USB.
product: Desk CO2 monitor with an OLED screen and a green-to-red light
mustHave: A true CO2 reading in ppm (an NDIR or photoacoustic sensor, not an eCO2 estimate from a VOC sensor)
A small screen that shows the CO2 number from a seated position at the desk
A light that goes green to red as the CO2 rises, visible from across the desk
Powered from USB (a phone charger or the computer)
Simple and cheap: one unit, built at home from off-the-shelf boards, no custom PCB
niceToHave: Temperature and humidity on the screen (the CO2 sensor measures both)
No soldering of fine-pitch parts; plug-together connectors where they exist
The case printable on an ordinary FDM printer or ordered from an online print service

constraints.power: USB 5 V into the controller's own USB socket; no battery
constraints.budgetBasis: assumed: the user said 'not expensive' and gave no number; under 100 USD all in (parts, print, shipping to Italy)
constraints.region: Italy (EU shops, EUR prices, duty on non-EU orders)
constraints.tools: soldering iron for through-hole and short-pitch SMD, heat-set insert tip or the iron itself, screwdrivers, a computer with a USB port
constraints.madeParts: FDM print in PLA or PETG, on a friend's printer or from an online print service
constraints.maxFootprintMm: about 70 x 30 on the desk (assumed: a small desk object)
